name: Bedrock Robotics Bedrock Operator
summary: A retrofit sensor and computer kit that lets 20–80 ton excavators dig and load trucks without an operator; so far used only with US partner contractors.

germany.statusNote: Not offered in Germany: Bedrock works with US partner contractors through an early-access programme, and its first fully autonomous deployments ran on US projects from August 2026. No European office, partner or price found.

specs.label: Host machines
specs.conditions: installed on several excavator models by November 2025; bulldozers, loaders and dump trucks planned

specs.label: Installation
specs.value: same-day retrofit without permanent changes to the machine

specs.label: Manual operation
specs.conditions: equipment can still be operated manually when needed

specs.label: Sensors and compute
specs.value: 360° cameras, LiDAR, survey-grade IMUs, GPS, LTE antennas, in-cab compute unit

specs.label: How it works
specs.value: a site manager sets the initial plan; a machine-learning model perceives the site, plans the motion and digs

specs.label: Safety
specs.value: stops automatically when a person or unauthorized object comes too close; no work-zone barriers needed

specs.label: Productivity
specs.conditions: company spokesperson, August 2026 deployments; measured as cubic yards moved per shift

notes: Only excavators so far; dump trucks, dozers and loaders are planned.
The current operator-free sites use new excavators that Bedrock outfitted and tested itself; no date was given for retrofits on contractors' own machines (September 2026).
A remote team monitors the fleet and steps in briefly when a machine gets stuck.
